source_text: Circa Felicitatem uero, et illi gratia domini eiusmodi contigit. Cum octo iam mensium uentrem haberet (nam praegnans fuerat adprehensa), instante spectaculi die in magno erat luctu, ne propter uentrem differretur (quia non licet praegnantes poenae repraesentari) et ne inter alios postea sceleratos sanctum et innocentem sanguinem funderet. Sed et commartyres grauiter contristabantur, ne tam bonam sociam quasi comitem solam in uia eiusdem spei relinquerent. Coniuncto itaque unito gemitu ad dominum orationem fuderunt ante tertium diem muneris. Et statim post orationem dolores inuaserunt. Et cum pro naturali difficultate octaui mensis in partu laborans doleret, ait illi quidam ex ministris cataractariorum: Quae sic modo doles, quid facies obiecta bestiis, quas contempsisti cum sacrificare noluisti? Et illa respondit: Modo ego patior quod patior; illic autem alius erit in me qui patietur pro me, quia et ego pro illo passura sum. Ita enixa est puellam, quam sibi quaedam soror in filiam educauit.
thought_title: Felicity gives birth in prison so she can die with the others
orientation: The editor continues the narrative after the visions by telling what happened to Felicity, the pregnant prisoner.
pass_a_gloss: But concerning Felicity, also to her the grace of the Lord of this kind happened. Since she already was having a belly of eight months (for pregnant she had been arrested), with the day of the show pressing on she was in great grief, lest on account of the belly she be put off (because it is not allowed for pregnant women to be presented for punishment) and lest afterwards among other criminals she pour out holy and innocent blood. But also her fellow martyrs were being gravely saddened, lest so good an ally as a companion they leave alone on the road of the same hope. With united groaning joined together therefore they poured out prayer to the Lord before the third day of the public games. And immediately after the prayer pains invaded her. And when, laboring in childbirth she was in pain on account of the natural difficulty of the eighth month, one from the attendants of the prison gatekeepers says to her: You who so suffer now, what will you do when thrown to the wild beasts, which you despised when you refused to sacrifice? And she answered: Now I suffer what I suffer; but there another will be in me who will suffer for me, because also I am about to suffer for him. Thus she bore a girl, whom a certain sister raised for herself as a daughter.

pass_b_english: As for Felicity, the grace of the Lord came to her in this way. She was eight months pregnant as the day of the spectacle drew near, for she had been arrested while pregnant, and she was in great distress for fear her punishment would be put off because of her pregnancy, since pregnant women may not be presented for punishment, and she would then shed her holy and innocent blood later among common criminals. Her fellow martyrs were also deeply grieved at the thought of leaving so good a comrade behind alone on the road of their shared hope.

So together they poured out a united prayer to the Lord with groaning three days before the public games. Labor pains seized her right after the prayer. As she struggled in childbirth, made harder by the natural difficulty of the eighth month, one of the prison gatekeepers said to her, "You suffer so much now, what will you do when you are thrown to the wild beasts, which you scorned when you refused to sacrifice?" She answered, "Now I suffer what I suffer. But there another will be in me who will suffer for me, because I too am about to suffer for him."
In this way she gave birth to a little girl, and one sister took the child to raise as her own daughter.
